first_impression: This looks lovely in the trailer shots. The title screen, the sunset cutaway over the pines at 03:27 and the snowy pass at 11:30 made me want to click right away. Then the actual play is a high camera looking down on a flat lawn while a tiny dog nudges a clump of white blobs, and that is less exciting. I like how each evening adds its own twist, but the herding underneath feels the same every time, and nothing seems to put real pressure on you.
best_things: The set pieces look gorgeous: the low sunset cutaways (03:27, 11:30), the low zoomed-in view of the meadow at 00:51-01:00, and the whole First Snow evening (10:54-12:42), with its white fields, a dark burn and a black sheep that stands out in the flock.

Every evening adds a real new rule with a clear briefing card. Old Angus the ram plants himself and you have to stare him down (05:09-05:36), the Glenbrae Trial has flagged fetch, drive and cross gates (01:24-02:51), Mist on the Moor makes you follow bleats, the Storm floods the ford, and the Night Watch counts down to dawn instead of nightfall.

The wolf snatch is staged well. You get a red banner with the distance and seconds left, a picture-in-picture of the wolf carrying the sheep, a red ring on the wolf on the ground, then gold rings and 'Sheep rescued!' when you get there (04:39-04:45, 10:15-10:24). The season board with stars, ribbons and charms (00:03, 01:18) gives me a reason to replay.

worst_problems.problem: Most of the time the camera hangs high over a flat field, so the animals are small, there is no horizon or sky, and the pretty world only shows in cutaways. The Trial especially is a featureless mustard lawn with diagonal shadow stripes for a minute and a half.
worst_problems.suggestion: Let me play closer and lower, like the 00:51 view, or at least zoom in. Give the field some landmarks, hedges, a crowd at the show field, a slope, so it doesn't look like a putting green.

worst_problems.problem: There are long dead stretches where nothing happens. At the trial pen the sheep mill around the gate while Pip paces back and forth. In Lambing Time Pip stands behind a still flock by the bridge for half a minute. In the Night Watch you circle a flock that is just sitting there.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make penning snappier (a stronger pull once they are at the mouth) and give quiet watches something to react to, like a straggler, a fox or a gust that spooks them, so I'm not waiting.

worst_problems.problem: The wolves never feel like much of a threat. The first evening ends with all 8 home and three stars about a minute after it starts. Snatches are saved within a few seconds, and the Night Watch ends with 'Not one lost'. The pitch promises tension at sundown, but every evening shown is a tidy win.
worst_problems.suggestion: Have packs that work together, wolves that circle and split the flock, and a harder tier for replays, so that losing a sheep is a real risk and a three-star night feels earned.

worst_problems.problem: At dusk the play view goes muddy. The ground turns rusty orange-brown with purple speckles, the sheep turn pink, and the mist evening is a brownish-lilac smear. The sunset looks great as a cutaway but murky where I actually play.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep the grass looking like grass and keep the sheep white at sunset. Let the sky glow and long shadows carry the mood instead of tinting the whole field.

worst_problems.problem: Some water looks broken. The flooded burn in the Storm reads as a black asphalt road with white lane dashes, the loch in Old Angus has a dark, blocky, stair-stepped edge, and the snowy burn is a smeary blur.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give the flood visible flow, foam and brown churned water so it reads as a river you cannot cross, and smooth out the loch shoreline.

boredom_points: Evening 1 (00:12-01:12) is over in about a minute with no challenge. It's a fine tutorial, but nothing about it hooks me.
Trying to get the last ewes into the trial pen (02:24-02:51) looks fiddly and slow: one sheep in, the rest standing at the mouth while Pip walks back and forth.
Lambing Time 04:00-04:36: Pip holds still behind the flock next to the bridge for over half a minute and the frames barely change.
Mist on the Moor 08:00-08:15: running along an empty track in fog with no sheep in view, just bleat icons stacked on the screen edge.
Night Watch 12:45-13:09: walking circles round a flock that is just sitting still in blue moonlight.
confusions: Why do the sheep turn pink at sunset (04:12, 07:51, 10:12)? At first I thought something had happened to them.
What are the big diagonal dark stripes across the trial field (01:24-02:51)? Shadows from trees I can't see, mown stripes, or something I should avoid?
In Lambing Time I couldn't tell lambs from ewes from that height (03:00-03:24), so 'keep each lamb with its mother' was hard to follow.
At 12:06-12:09 a wall of giant pines fills the lower half of the screen and I lost Pip behind them.
In the mist, the left edge stacks three sheep icons (08:00-08:06). I couldn't tell which way each group was or how far.
Is the low zoomed-in view at 00:51-01:00 something I can play in, or only a camera trick?
What is the 'Friday's Evening' card on the season board (00:03, 01:18)?
wish_list: A playable low or close camera, or free zoom, so I can see Pip and the sheep up close while herding.
Whistle-style commands (come-bye, away, walk on) or a more expressive dog with a proper herding crouch and eye.
A harder replay mode or extra ribbons with smarter wolf packs, for people who three-star everything.
A farmhouse hub between evenings where you can pet Pip, see the flock grow and spend charms.
Photo mode, because the sunsets and snow deserve it.
one_line_review: Gorgeous, gentle sheepdog game with a clever new twist every evening, but from up in the sky it often feels like pushing cotton balls across a lawn while the wolves barely bite.
